Polyandry

By: Eugene Botha | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Will marriage laws make it possible for wives to have more than one husband?

Unique Selling Point:
Proposed new legislation that is creating quite a stir nationally and internationally...

Summary:
The country’s marriage laws could in the near future allow women to marry more than one husband, just as polygamous men can have many wives. The legalisation of polyandry is one of the wide-ranging proposals in a Green Paper on Marriages gazetted by the Department of Home Affairs last week.

Further information:
The country’s marriage laws could in the near future allow women to marry more than one husband, just as polygamous men can have many wives.Legalisation of polyandry is one of the wide-ranging proposals in a Green Paper on Marriages gazetted by the Department of Home Affairs last week.

The Green Paper aims to work towards the development of a new Single Marriage Bill and will align the country’s marriage regime with the constitutional principle of equality. The Department wrote that the envisaged marriage statute will enable South Africans and residents of all sexual orientations, religions and cultural persuasions to conclude legal marriages that will accord with the principles of equality, non-discrimination, human dignity and unity in diversity, as encapsulated in the Constitution.

This is necessary because currently South Africa’s marriage laws are a weird mixed bag. For instance, the current legislation does not regulate some religious marriages such as the Hindu, Muslim and other customary marriages that are practised in some African or royal families. It also does not legislate for a variety of permutations in terms of identity and sexual orientation, such as marriage between transgender persons, etc.

BUT THE ABSOLUTE GENDER EQUALITY IN THE LEGISLATION ALSO CREATED A MASSIVE CONTROVERSY, AND A DELIGHTFUL SPAT IN PARLIAMENT.
The legislation also opens the way for women to legally marry more than one husband.

And this many of the supporters of absolute gender equality (on paper) could not accept at all. We are all for equality and support polygamy, they shouted. But women do not have the right to do as men do! We can marry more than one woman, but they are not allowed to marry more than one man!

It also played out in Parliament where the DA’s Natasha Mazzone and Al-Jama’ah’s Ganief Hendricks:
During a plenary hybrid sitting of parliament on Tuesday, Hendricks said he was concerned by the polyandrous marriage proposal in the green paper.

“I am very concerned by the provision in the green paper of the Marriage Act where women are allowed to take more than one husband. You can imagine when a child is born, more DNA tests will be needed to discover who the father is. The problem is only going to get worse,” Hendricks said
An outraged Mazzone responded to Hendricks' comments, saying they were insulting to every woman.
Mazzone said Hendricks should be investigated by the parliamentary ethics committee.
“I would like you to refer to what the last speaker, who I will not refer to as honourable, has just said. He was insulting to every woman in this country regarding the rights of women to have multiple husbands and the rights of men to have multiple wives. It is not right, in 2021, to have people in Parliament says disgraceful things like that. He will be referred to the Ethics Committee. The only woman who could possibly agree with him in this country, is his own wife, ” said Mazzone.
And Ganief Hendricks is not a lone voice. It was especially political parties which draw their support from religious voters, that have slammed this proposed change to South Africa’s marriage laws.
And they were soon joined by a number of religious organizations, representing millions of South Africans. They all have serious objections to the proposed legislation.
This proposal is for a story on the proposed changes in the Act with a focus on the contentious issue of women being allowed to have multiple husbands.

Natasha Mazzone
Ganief Hendricks

Press Release:


Easier Wed than Done

Cabinet has agreed to publication of the Green Paper on Marriages in South Africa for public consultation. In it, a Single Marriage Bill is proposed that will seek to align South Africa’s complex marriage regime with the constitutional principles of equality, non-discrimination, dignity, as well as cultural and religious freedom. In the spirit of absolute gender equality, the new legislation would open the way for women to legally marry more than one husband. The suggestion that polyandry might be legalised has been met with offence and outrage from several quarters. While the final legislation will look quite different post the public consultation process which closes on 30 June, Carte Blanche investigates what the draft says about the evolution of South African society.

Producer: Eugene Botha | Presenter: Claire Mawisa

Script:


Elizabeth:
In my value system honesty is what matters. Whether or not you have more than one sexual partner, it is what you are honest about.
V/O:
Elizabeth Retief lives in Cape Town and is a therapist. She is also part of a growing number of South Africans who subscribe to the notion of polyamory.
Elizabeth:
Polyamory is a form of consensual non-monogamy or ethical non-monogamy both terms apply.
V/O:
And what this means for he, is that she finds fulfilment in having a loving, intimate, relationship with two people simultaneously.
Elizabeth:
The ethical component is essential. Everyone knows what’s happening, everyone talks about what they’re ok or not ok with. Everything is discussed, everything is above board.
V/O:
In addition, in polyamory there are no prescriptive gender roles, and no fixed relationship structures. It varies from relationship to relationship. Retief chooses not to live with her partners.
Elizabeth:
I am involved with a woman who is married and she lives with her husband, but I also got another partner who lives a couple of kilometres away and we see each other regularly and you just you now, the same way you manage two friendships you manage two relationships.
V/O:
Within this context there are women who have two male life partners. And because the polyamory community values privacy, this relationship model has not been the subject of public scrutiny. But, this changed two weeks ago.
LINK:
The possibility of one woman having two husbands at the same time became part of our national discourse recently. And there is even a name for it! It is called polyandry.
V/O:
This word pops up in a Green Paper on Marriages gazetted on then 4th of May in which proposals for new marital legislation are published for discussion. However, the Green paper and the term polyandry gained national prominence in a parliamentary debate on the backlog in DNA testing when Mr Ganief Hendricks of the Al Jama’h party took the podium.
Hendricks in Parliament
I’m very concerned about the provision in the green paper of the marriage act where women are allowed to take more than one husband so you can image when a baby is born, more DNA testing will be needed to determine who the father is.
V/O:
This was met with an angry response from Natasha Mazzone, the Chief Whip of the DA.
Natahsa in Parliament
I would like to refer to what the last speaker, who I will not refer to, has just said and how insulting it is to every woman in this country. Regarding to the rights of women to have multiple husbands.
LINK:
This altercation attracted a lot of attention to the proposed new legislation and created quite a stir nationwide.
V/O:
Shadi Maganoe, a lecturer at the Wits School of Law says the Green Paper was designed to address a very unsatisfactory situation in South African marital legislation. The fact that many cultural and religious marriages are not recognized is the main concern.
Shadi:
In terms of religious marriages, Hindu marriages are not recognised under the marriages act, Islam marriages as well as the Khoi-San marriages are not recognized.
V/O:
And where marriages are not recognized it is especially women who do not enjoy legal protection. In addition, the legislation that governs marriages in South Africa is very complex, consisting of many pieces of legislation.
Shadi:
We have different legislation for different marriages, so I think the different legislature right now is trying to harmonise all the marriages and put them under one legislation. So instead of having the recognition of customary marriages, the civil union act, the marriage act, which doesn’t even cover all the different types of marriages in South Africa, the legislator is trying to harmonise all of these different types of marriages under one legislation.
V/O:
And the proposals also aim to align marriage legislation with key principles in the constitution such as equality, dignity and non-discrimination. It also proposes the abolition of child marriages. Mazzone supports this, especially the idea of equality where it comes to marital models.
Natasha:
But I also believe that what is good for the goose is good for the gander, so if we are going to allow for multiple wives in our country in the case of men, then of course we it is only fair to allow for multiple husbands, should a woman want one. I don’t think it is something that we should allow culture or religious practices to stand in the way of, Our constitution must reign supreme and equality is at stake here.
V/O:
However, Hendricks finds this unacceptable because in Islam God is seen the initiator of marriage and only monogamy or polygamy, where a man is allowed more than one wife is allowed in their sacred book the Koran.
Ganief:
My personal view is that the Green Paper must be thrown in a wastepaper basket. So, we don’t want parliament to vote on the tenets of our religion and I’m very sure many other religions wouldn’t want a parliament to vote on their divine scriptures.
V/O:
And it seems the Muslim community is far from alone in their objection against polyandry.
LINK:
And for many Christians the idea of polyandry is also totally unacceptable.
V/O:
The African Christian Democratic Party has come out strongly against polyandry, and Bishop Marothi Mashashane of the National Christian Forum, an organization with a membership of two hundred and forty-three Churches, is adamant that polyandry goes against their Christian beliefs.
Mashashane:
Our position is very straight and very unshaken, we believe that God is the author of the institution called marriage, the principles are very simple, God is saying a man and a woman, so there is no other formula that we are going to support, out of the word of God, out of the Bible, that we believe on.
V/O:
He says the National Christian Forum has already submitted their objections to the proposed new legislation to Parliament and will not allow the legislation to pass.
LINK:
Apart from religious concerns, objections against polyandry have also been raised by those who believe it goes against the grain of many traditional cultures.
V/O:
This past Tuesday the ANC in KZN released a statement, voicing their rejection of polyandry.
V/O:
Musa Mseleku, reality television star and businessman, who has four wives, agrees, but says that is not because he denies the importance of equality.
Musa:
When we take one wife it’s not that because we want to show some kind of power, or we want to cling to some kind of patriarchy.
V/O:
He says the notion of polyandry is un-African and as such jeopardizes cultural traditions and will bring confusion in terms of lineage and property, and it would cast age old gender roles into disarray.
Musa:. I am of the opinion that women, they wont be able to carry this responsibility.
V/O:
The gap between what lawmakers propose and what religious and cultural leaders will accept is wide, but Mazzone is confident that it can be bridged.
Natasha:
But I think it is going to take a meeting between our cultural and religious leaders, together with our lawmakers, and out constitution needs to reign supreme. So, we need to look at the principles of our constitution, that fundamentally form the principles of all our law.
Question:
What are your thoughts on the Green Paper? Is it a move in the right direction?

Elizabeth:
I think it is absolutely a move in the right direction for its main purpose, which is to protect women who are currently stuck in traditional marriages without legal protection. It’s not right at the moment, that there is a legal avenue that gives rights and advantages, that is not available to everyone.
V/O:
And Retief says new legislation will also benefit the polyamorous community in South Africa.
Elizabeth:
It is not like everyone in the polyamorous community will rush out to get married, many people are not interested in that at all, but there are people who would very much like to have that option.
She also says ample research has shown that Polyamory is not harmful to children and polyandry can work. Even the practicalities around things like jealousy is not a major issue in these types of relationships.
Elizabeth
It is just an uncomfortable emotion. And jealousy, you know, there’s different things that lie behind jealousy and there are ways to work with jealousy.
LINK:
The debate the last few weeks has been quite intense, but one must remember that the Green Paper is a discussion document and members of the public have until the end of June to respond to the proposals.
Shadi:
It is not law, it is not a commitment. It is just the government trying to consult with the public as to what are you thinking on these things.
V/O:
And Maganoe adds that in these deliberations one must be aware of the presuppositions that we are bringing to the table where it concerns something like polyandry.
Shadi:
Are we imposing our Western practices into our religious practices or into our cultural practices, so it is not always that simple or always that black and white. Those are the questions we need to ask ourselves every time you try to develop either indigenous law or if you are trying to develop religion to conform to the provisions of the bill of rights.

metadata.Summary: The country’s marriage laws could in the near future allow women to marry more than one husband, just as polygamous men can have many wives. metadata.Further information: The country’s marriage laws could in the near future allow women to marry more than one husband, just as polygamous men can have many wives.Legalisation of polyandry is one of the wide-ranging proposals in a Green Paper on Marriages gazetted by the Department of Home Affairs last week. The Green Paper aims to work towards the development of a new Single Marriage Bill and will align the country’s marriage regime with the constitutional principle of equality. The Department wrote that the envisaged marriage statute will enable South Africans and residents of all sexual orientations, religions and cultural persuasions to conclude legal marriages that will accord with the principles of equality, non-discrimination, human dignity and unity in diversity, as encapsulated in the Constitution. This is necessary because currently South Africa’s marriage laws are a weird mixed bag. For instance, the current legislation does not regulate some religious marriages such as the Hindu, Muslim and other customary marriages that are practised in some African or royal families. It also does not legislate for a variety of permutations in terms of identity and sexual orientation, such as marriage between transgender persons, etc. BUT THE ABSOLUTE GENDER EQUALITY IN THE LEGISLATION ALSO CREATED A MASSIVE CONTROVERSY, AND A DELIGHTFUL SPAT IN PARLIAMENT. The legislation also opens the way for women to legally marry more than one husband. And this many of the supporters of absolute gender equality (on paper) could not accept at all. We are all for equality and support polygamy, they shouted. But women do not have the right to do as men do! We can marry more than one woman, but they are not allowed to marry more than one man! It also played out in Parliament where the DA’s Natasha Mazzone and Al-Jama’ah’s Ganief Hendricks: During a plenary hybrid sitting of parliament on Tuesday, Hendricks said he was concerned by the polyandrous marriage proposal in the green paper. “I am very concerned by the provision in the green paper of the Marriage Act where women are allowed to take more than one husband. You can imagine when a child is born, more DNA tests will be needed to discover who the father is. The problem is only going to get worse,” Hendricks said An outraged Mazzone responded to Hendricks' comments, saying they were insulting to every woman. Mazzone said Hendricks should be investigated by the parliamentary ethics committee. “I would like you to refer to what the last speaker, who I will not refer to as honourable, has just said. He was insulting to every woman in this country regarding the rights of women to have multiple husbands and the rights of men to have multiple wives. It is not right, in 2021, to have people in Parliament says disgraceful things like that. He will be referred to the Ethics Committee. The only woman who could possibly agree with him in this country, is his own wife, ” said Mazzone. And Ganief Hendricks is not a lone voice. It was especially political parties which draw their support from religious voters, that have slammed this proposed change to South Africa’s marriage laws. And they were soon joined by a number of religious organizations, representing millions of South Africans. They all have serious objections to the proposed legislation. This proposal is for a story on the proposed changes in the Act with a focus on the contentious issue of women being allowed to have multiple husbands. The following people could be interviewed: Natasha Mazzone Ganief Hendricks Bishop Marothi Mashashane Musa Mseleku Elizabeth Retief, Polyamorist Shadi Maganoe of Wits
